what: the campaign's 99.2594 % coverage ceiling is wrong on its own logic, and the same default-off flag explains both directions of the error.

the_claim_being_corrected.says: the ceiling on device-measured coverage is 99.2594 %, because 0.74055 % of the model's gradient mass is on a weight applied on the host after a ttnn.to_torch, so no device gradient for it exists
the_claim_being_corrected.and_says: why_this_is_not_a_defect: 'Closing it would require porting the op, not fixing a number.'
the_claim_being_corrected.also_says: the diffusion arm's unreached 1.1286 % is RECOVERABLE by measurement

error_one_the_class_is_bigger_than_the_c.carrier: perf/of3t_readable_mass/READABLE_MASS.json, of3t-readable-mass, a namespace outside this row's and outside the orchestrator's
error_one_the_class_is_bigger_than_the_c.why: the ceiling counted the input_embedder side only. READABLE_MASS resolves the same class over BOTH prefixes it is defined by -- diffusion_module.atom_attn_enc.ref_atom_feature_embedder. and input_embedder.atom_attn_enc.ref_atom_feature_embedder. -- plus input_embedder.atom_attn_enc.linear_q.0.weight, 17 tensors. The diffusion side's 0.75304 % is the same host-applied class and the ceiling does not count it, while COVERAGE_CEILING separately lists the diffusion arm's unreached 1.1286 % as RECOVERABLE. 0.75304 of that 1.1286 is host-applied, so it is not recoverable by measurement on the ceiling's own reasoning.
error_one_the_class_is_bigger_than_the_c.so: on its own premise the ceiling is 98.47976 %, not 99.2594 %, a 0.77964-point overstatement.

error_two_the_class_is_not_structural_at.the_flag: TT_BIO_OF3_DEVICE_REFATOM, tt_bio/openfold3_host_prep.py:187, env_flag(..., False) -- DEFAULT OFF
error_two_the_class_is_not_structural_at.what_the_source_says: the comment at that definition: 'On, the eight ref_atom_feature_embedder linears and the input embedder's linear_q.0.weight run WHERE A COTANGENT CAN REACH THEM -- which is what HOST_APPLIED names in perf/of3t_readable_mass/READABLE_MASS.json.' The flag names the very class by name.

both_sides_are_wired.diffusion_side: tt_bio/worker.py:1559-1565 -- rafe_sd = _sub(model.sd, 'diffusion_module.atom_attn_enc.ref_atom_feature_embedder'); if env_flag(DEVICE_REF_ATOM, False): cl0_d, plm0_d = ref_atom_embed_device(...) else: cl0, plm0 = ref_atom_embed(...). The device replica is openfold3_host_prep.ref_atom_embed_device at line 262.
both_sides_are_wired.input_embedder_side: tt_bio/openfold3_host_prep.py:322 -- the same flag swaps the linear_q aggregation head onto the card via openfold3.AtomEncoderTokenHead, and the comment there names linear_q.0.weight as 0.74055 % of the model's squared gradient norm, the ceiling's exact number.

error_two_the_class_is_not_structural_at.so: the op is PORTED and closing the class is a FLAG, not porting work. COVERAGE_CEILING's 'Closing it would require porting the op, not fixing a number' is incorrect as of the live tree.
error_two_the_class_is_not_structural_at.note: READ_ON_ANOTHER_BOUNDARY (5.82817 %, the pairformer stack) is not a blocker of the same kind: a device gradient for it exists, on the trunk boundary.

the_caveat_that_keeps_the_flag_off.why_default_off: the source states it: 'a device linear in bf16 or fp32 is not bit-identical to the host float32 one it replaces, and the OF3T charter's hard constraint is that nothing may change inference's output or slow it down.'
the_caveat_that_keeps_the_flag_off.so: the flag must stay default-off for INFERENCE, and this row does not propose moving it. It costs nothing in production to turn it on inside a MEASUREMENT instrument, which is the only thing recommended here. Release-gated, not shipped.

what_it_is_worth_to_THIS_row.what_that_needs: NOT just the env var. The flag is wired on the shipped fold path (worker.py, openfold3_fold.py); the trajectory harness builds OF3DiffusionModule directly and feeds its own inputs, so it would have to call ref_atom_embed_device itself and register those 8 weights in the walked parameter set. That is wiring in the harness, not a port, and the eligibility check matters: the flag existing is not the flag firing on this path.
what_it_is_worth_to_THIS_row.cost: one re-run of the diffusion trajectory's two sides, priced in FLOOR.json at 3.44 h as paid on qb2 at OMP 3, or about 1.9 h at 16 threads.

recommendation: restate the coverage ceiling. On its own logic it is 98.47976 %, not 99.2594 %. With TT_BIO_OF3_DEVICE_REFATOM on inside the instruments it is 100 % minus the 0.49476 % that FUSED_NOT_SPLIT, NO_ARM, NOT_A_LEAF_LAZY and ARM_RAN_DID_NOT_CARRY hold.
drop the sentence 'Closing it would require porting the op, not fixing a number' -- the op is ported and the number is a flag.
reclassify the 0.75304 % of the diffusion arm's 1.1286 % unreached mass from RECOVERABLE BY MEASUREMENT to HOST_APPLIED, which is the class READABLE_MASS already puts it in.
run the gradient and trajectory instruments with the flag ON, and keep it default-off for inference where the bit-identity constraint applies.
the_lesson: a ceiling stated as structural stopped anyone re-testing it for at least 175 passes of orchestration, and the thing that closes it is an env var named in a source comment that cites the very artifact the ceiling was computed from. The ceiling and its remedy were in the same repository the whole time.
